Subject: Clarify: how hosted API p95 is measured across nightly backup windows

Sergio —

Quick question as we're finalizing the ops checklist for our pilot: Atlas runs an I/O-heavy DB backup window nightly (02:00-03:30 UTC). We anticipate a surge of inference requests immediately after that window as batch jobs kick off. In your SLO language you describe p50/p95 measured over a "measurement epoch", but the doc isn't clear about how transient spikes immediately following scheduled maintenance are handled.

Specifically: if p95 is evaluated over a 24h epoch and one 10-minute spike from the backup-induced burst tips the percentile, will that count against Redwood's commitment or is there a carve-out? For contract negotiations we need something we can represent in our internal compliance review — ideally deterministic rules.

Can you outline the proposed epoch boundary, any transient carveouts you support, and a suggested trial period to validate behavior?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Platform, AtlasHealth
sam.patel@atlashealth.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: AtlasHealth SRE <sre@atlashealth.com>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: how hosted API p95 is measured across nightly backup windows

Sam —

Thanks for the clear note and for sharing the schedule. High level answer: we measure p50/p95 per defined 24h measurement epochs, but we support a small set of deterministic carveouts for operator-driven maintenance.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Measurement epoch: UTC 00:00-23:59 (24h rolling epochs aligned to UTC days).
- Transient maintenance carveout: any scheduled maintenance window that is declared >24h in advance and registered in our maintenance calendar is eligible for a limited carveout for SLO evaluation. The carveout removes the impacted time slice from the epoch numerator/denominator for aggregation.
- Burst smoothing/epoch boundary rule: If a spike begins within 10 minutes after a declared maintenance end, we attach that 10-minute period to the maintenance carveout to avoid penalty for immediate catch-up load. This is applied only when the spike pattern correlates with the declared maintenance.

Operational/contract terms we propose for Atlas:
1) We accept a temporary SLO deviation for p95 (hosted API) limited to the nightly backup period plus a 10-minute immediate-post window for a 30-day pilot starting 2027-02-05.
2) During the pilot, both parties will collect detailed traces and token-level latency breakdowns. If we observe persistent unmet commitments outside those carveouts, Redwood will propose remediation steps (routing changes, short-term burst capacity) to bring measured p95 back in line.
3) Post-pilot, we can either remove the carveout (if Atlas optimizes the burst) or formalize it as a permanent limited exception with a small price adjustment (volume-based).

I've attached a short "proposed-epoch-spec" that formalizes the carveout language and how we compute p95 with the exclusion window. If you'd like, I can route this to Legal/Procurement with a one-paragraph addendum for the current term sheet.

Next steps: confirm you want the 30-day pilot starting 2027-02-05 and I'll create the tracking DocuSign and a shared drive for traces.

Best —
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-02T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify: how hosted API p95 is measured across nightly backup windows — need approval to grant 30d deviation

Kim / Ben —

Forwarding the ask from Atlas (thread above). Summary: Atlas wants a deterministic carveout tied to their scheduled nightly DB backup (02:00-03:30 UTC) plus a 10-minute post-maintenance smoothing. They want this active for a 30-day pilot starting 2027-02-05 so they can validate our measurements.

Why this is reasonable: Atlas will share trace-level telemetry and has agreed to joint post-mortem if we see out-of-carveout regressions. We can implement the carveout in our SLO evaluation pipeline quickly by tagging the maintenance window; no runtime change needed.

Questions for approvals:
- Pricing impact: conservative estimate is a small uplift to committed spend if we formalize beyond the pilot. For a 30-day pilot we should make it promotional (no price change).
- Legal: the carveout language in the attached PDF is intentionally narrow — limited to scheduled maintenance with >24h notice and applied only to host-level artifacts correlated with declared maintenance.

Proposed internal action: approve the 30-day pilot with no price change, allow SRE traces to be shared to support measurement. If agreed I'll prepare the DocuSign addendum and copy Legal for visibility.

Thoughts?

— Sergio

On a related note: if we need short-term burst capacity during the pilot we can enable Dedicated burst seats for Atlas at short notice (they've signaled interest).

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick and concrete proposal. We accept the 30-day pilot starting 2027-02-05 with the carveout as you described (02:00-03:30 UTC plus 10-minute smoothing). We'll share the detailed traces and correlate them with the maintenance calendar entries.

Please send the DocuSign addendum and the shared Drive link for traces. Also note: our Procurement needs a written line in the addendum that the carveout is only valid for scheduled windows with >24h notice and cannot be applied retroactively. The attached schedule CSV is authoritative for our declared times for the pilot month.

Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to validating this with real telemetry.

Regards,
Sam
Head of Platform, AtlasHealth
